headline: Boston School Janitor Donates Kidney to Stranger
meta_description: A night janitor at a Boston school gave a kidney to a stranger, enabling a teacher's brother to receive a transplant.
summary_short: Andrew Allen, who cleans a Boston school at night, donated a kidney to a stranger so a teacher's brother could receive the transplant he needed.
body:
Andrew Allen works the night shift cleaning a Boston school. When he learned that a teacher at the school could not donate a kidney to his brother, Allen made an extraordinary choice: he donated one of his own kidneys to a stranger instead, freeing up a kidney for the teacher's brother through a transplant chain.

Allen's decision set in motion a cascade of medical hope. By giving his kidney to someone else in need, he created an opening in the transplant system that allowed the teacher's brother to receive the organ he desperately needed. It was an act of profound generosity from someone who works quietly behind the scenes at the school, cleaning its halls each night.

The donation reflects the quiet dignity many janitors bring to their work, often unseen. Allen's choice reminds us that acts of life-saving kindness can come from anyone, anywhere—even from those performing the most humble jobs in our communities.
